__comment: Dwarf name component pools for procedural generation.
GENERATION MODEL:
Every dwarf receives a single given name constructed as:
name = prefix + suffix
Male and female pools are separate — different phoneme patterns.
Male names lean on hard stops and voiced fricatives (Brom-, Dur-, Grun-).
Female names lean on softer endings and liquid consonants (Brun-, Kel-, Sol-).
Pool sizes:
Male:   25 prefixes × 20 suffixes = 500 distinct names
Female: 25 prefixes × 20 suffixes = 500 distinct names
Total:  1 000 distinct names (500 per gender)
UNIQUENESS HANDLING:
The generator tracks used names in the current world. If a rolled combination
has already been assigned, it re-rolls up to 10 times before falling back to
appending the dwarf's birth-order index as a Roman numeral suffix
(e.g. 'Bromin II'). This fallback is expected to be extremely rare — at the
point where ~500 same-gender dwarves have been generated the pool is
effectively exhausted, which requires a very long-running colony.
Name generation uses the world seed as its RNG root so the same world always
produces the same sequence of dwarf names in the same order.
PHONEME NOTES:
Not every prefix+suffix pair is equally euphonic — that is intentional.
Dwarven names in this world are guttural and idiosyncratic. A name like
'Snoruk' or 'Bogorn' is as valid as 'Thorin' or 'Durmar'.
